chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Jamming and emceeing in the Florida lounge; Wells invites him to Harlem
summary: He started jamming and emceeing in the lounge with visiting stars, got another eight weeks, and Wells of Wells' Chicken Shack invited him to Harlem.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, when I get off from work I come home from the beach and I would start jammin' in the lounge and I'd start doin' the same thing I was doin' in the Paradise, because I did it for nothin'. Because I just wanted to blow; I didn't want to go to bed. Everybody's in town, Jimmy Durante or Sammy Davis or Louis (Armstrong) or Nat King Cole, Billy Eckstine, everybody was in. And they would all come there, when they got off from work. So I became the M.C. and, you know, and so we created somethin'. So then the manager said, "Well look here, why don't you come on in here, bring your band?" So we went

on in there and I worked there another eight weeks. So, in other words, it worked out all right. (laughter) Then Wells, of Wells Chicken Shack, you know, he's been up there (Harlem) for years. He was down (in Florida) on vacation and so Austin Powell and I... Austin and I stayed and we got local fellows to play the rhythm and so Wells says, "Look here, why don't you come up to my place in Harlem?" So when we left down there we went right on up and worked in Wells' Chicken Shack and at different times I had Oscar Pettiford on bass, Al McKibbon, Hank Jones was playin' piano there for a long time. In fact, he married Wells' secretary when he was there. And the guys would come in and jam and I must have stood up there over a year. Yeah. Of course Austin is an entertainer and we were doin' some things together and people liked us, so that was a nice job. Yeah.
